solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Male with inclination to engage in securing deliveries? (4,7)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is the art of bowling such deliveries, so the plural noun stands loosely for the activity

indicatorNotes.to engage in: to engage is to mesh with or enter, as gears engage, so M and BOW enter SEALING

blocks.note: a bow is an inclination of the head or body
sealing a parcel is securing it

annotation.surface: A man with a leaning towards the job of securing parcels for delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: The deliveries are cricket ones, not parcels: seam bowling makes the ball deviate off its raised stitching (the seam) when it pitches.
annotation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowled ball is a delivery, and seam bowling is one whole style of producing them, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Political advisor upset after party member’s debut in online fora (6,5)

indicatorNotes.upset: to upset is literally to tip over, and in a down entry a word tipped over reads bottom to top
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the tipped-over word follows the rest
indicatorNotes.debut: a debut is a first appearance, so the member appears only as its first letter

annotation.surface: A political aide gets upset about a party member's first posts on internet forums.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Political advisor upset' reads as a person in a temper; it is AIDE turned over, and it goes last.
annotation.definitionFit: Fora is the Latin plural of forum, and social media sites are where the public now gathers to debate, as in a forum.

entries.clue: Eighteen letters defending prelude of classical performer (5)

indicatorNotes.defending: defenders stand round what they protect, so A TO R stands round the C
indicatorNotes.prelude: a prelude is what comes before the main piece, so only the first letter

blocks.note: A TO R: the alphabet from A to R is eighteen letters

annotation.surface: A classical performer defending eighteen letters, as if in a spelling contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eighteen letters' is not a count to satisfy but a span of the alphabet: A to R, written A TO R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who performs roles in plays or films.

entries.clue: Assistance for mooring lines pushed through side of ship (7)

indicatorNotes.pushed through: something pushed through a board ends up inside it, so the lines sit within BOARD

blocks.note: board = a ship's side, as in overboard and starboard

annotation.surface: Mooring ropes are fed through holes in a ship's side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mooring lines' looks like one phrase; the definition stops at 'mooring' and 'lines' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: the short post on a quay that ropes are looped round helps a boat moor.

entries.clue: Prosecute comedian over conclusion to joke (4)

indicatorNotes.over: over means above, and in a down entry the comedian sits above the E
indicatorNotes.conclusion: the conclusion of anything is its end, so the last letter of joke

annotation.surface: Taking a comedian to court over the punchline of a joke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prosecute' reads as legal; here it means to carry on, as in to prosecute or wage a war.
annotation.definitionFit: Prosecute has an older sense, to carry on or pursue, as in prosecuting a war, which is to wage it.

entries.clue: Remorseless boxer, Ali, dancing, keeping mostly fresh (10)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers move about the floor, so the letters of BOXER ALI move out of order
indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so the mixed letters hold NE
indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: NEW, fresh, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Muhammad Ali, the relentless boxer, dancing round the ring and keeping himself fresh.
annotation.walkthrough: Ali really did dance, so 'dancing' reads as description; it is the instruction to rearrange BOXER ALI.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: what cannot be stopped or moved by pleading is without remorse or pity.

entries.clue: Castaway genius repurposed coastal rocks (6,8)

indicatorNotes.repurposed: something repurposed is remade for a new use, so the letters are remade into a new phrase

annotation.surface: A brilliant shipwrecked sailor finds new uses for the rocks on his shore.
annotation.walkthrough: The Giant's Causeway is a headland of hexagonal basalt columns on the coast of Northern Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the landmark is tens of thousands of basalt columns stepping into the sea off County Antrim.

entries.clue: Gaze a long time on story involving female’s elevated status? (4,7)

indicatorNotes.on: on means following on after, so the gazing and the long time come after the story
indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to enfold, so the story LIE enfolds the F

blocks.note: an age is a long time

annotation.surface: Staring for ages at a tale about a woman who rose in society.
annotation.walkthrough: A life peerage is a British title for the holder's lifetime only, raising them to the House of Lords; hence 'elevated'.
annotation.definitionFit: Being made a peer is called elevation to the peerage, so the rank is literally an elevated status.

entries.clue: Girl working to outlaw foremost activity in rodeo (8)

indicatorNotes.to outlaw foremost: to outlaw is to ban, so the foremost letter is banned from the word

blocks.note: DOING, working, without its first letter D

annotation.surface: A girl campaigning to ban the leading event at a rodeo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working' is DOING, not ON or GOING; banning its first letter leaves OING.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: roping calves with a thrown loop is one of the standard rodeo events.

entries.clue: Criminal to engage in swordplay (5)

blocks.note: a noun here: a crook who buys and sells stolen goods
the verb for fighting with foils or sabres as a sport

annotation.surface: A crook who picks sword fights.
annotation.walkthrough: The criminal sense is a receiver of stolen goods, so 'Criminal' is a noun here, not an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for a receiver of stolen property, and the verb for the Olympic sword sport.

entries.clue: A lot of newspaper copy leading to editor’s first decree (9)

indicatorNotes.A lot of: a lot of something is much but not all of it, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.leading to: what leads to something comes before it, so the E comes last
indicatorNotes.first: the editor's first is the first letter of the word editor

blocks.note: PRESS, the newspapers, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Lots of copied newspaper text leads to the editor's first ruling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copy' is a verb, CRIB, not the newspaper noun it seems to be beside 'newspaper'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to lay down with authority what must be done.

entries.clue: Attention was curtailed by problem in hearing? (6)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: to curtail is to cut short, and 'cur-tail' suggests docking the tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to give ear is to pay attention
x = by, as in 3 x 4, 'three by four'

annotation.surface: Attention span was cut short by a hearing problem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link but supplies X, the multiplication sign read as 'by'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a plug of this can block the ear canal and dull hearing, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Broadway show using thematic lilt in a new way (1,6,5,5)

indicatorNotes.in a new way: doing something in a new way means changing its arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A Broadway musical rearranging its signature tune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'using' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sondheim's 1973 musical opened on Broadway.

entries.clue: Electricity row ensnaring one party representative (11)

indicatorNotes.ensnaring: a snare traps what walks into it, so TIER traps ONE in its middle

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

annotation.surface: An argument about electricity bills catches one party's spokesperson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line of seats, TIER, not a quarrel as the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A campaigner who canvasses votes on behalf of a political party at election time.

entries.clue: Gallery publication possibly providing art analogies on cue (9,8)

indicatorNotes.possibly: possibly means the letters could be something else, so they can be rearranged

annotation.surface: A gallery booklet offers comparisons between artworks exactly when needed.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is French, 'reasoned catalogue', and the entry drops the accent on the final E.
annotation.definitionFit: A complete annotated list of an artist's works, the kind of scholarly book galleries and museums publish.

entries.clue: European river starts to run here in East (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the words run and here are their opening letters

blocks.note: first letters of Run and Here

annotation.surface: A European river rises at this point in the east.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container instruction; it goes into the answer as written.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it flows from the Swiss Alps through Germany to the North Sea.

entries.clue: Right to avoid description of motorway for description of flying (6)

indicatorNotes.to avoid: to avoid something is to keep out of its way, so the letters of RT are kept out

blocks.note: a motorway is an arterial road

annotation.surface: A roads official avoids calling motorways one thing, preferring a word for flight.
annotation.walkthrough: The two letters of the abbreviation are not side by side in the longer word, but both go.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective for anything done in the air, like aerial acrobatics or aerial combat.

entries.clue: Additional comment: cowboy’s sidekick recalled stabbing enemy (8)

indicatorNotes.recalled: to recall is literally to call back, so the name is read back to front
indicatorNotes.stabbing: a stabbing blade goes into its victim, so the reversed name goes into FOE

blocks.note: TONTO, the Lone Ranger's sidekick, reversed

annotation.surface: A note added to a Western: the cowboy's sidekick remembered knifing an enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: Tonto is the Lone Ranger's companion in the Western series.
annotation.definitionFit: A note printed at the foot of a page adds a comment to the main text.

entries.clue: Small bird — horse pursued by it around area (4,3)

indicatorNotes.pursued by: a pursuer runs behind, so IT comes after the horse
indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the horse's letters surround A

blocks.note: a colt is a young horse

annotation.surface: A small bird flits round a paddock where a horse is chased.
annotation.walkthrough: A coal tit is a small European songbird of the tit family.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the smallest of the tits, a family of tiny songbirds.

entries.clue: No magical individual in Hogwarts had finally brought in prohibited items (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the non-magical person is placed in between the two letters
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so the final letters of Hogwarts and had

blocks.note: a Muggle is a non-magical person in Harry Potter
last letters of HogwartS and haD

annotation.surface: Hogwarts finally let in a non-wizard who carried in forbidden things.
annotation.walkthrough: Hogwarts is the wizarding school in the Harry Potter books, where non-magical people are Muggles.
annotation.definitionFit: To smuggle is to carry contraband secretly across a border or into a place.

entries.clue: Smooth surface I start to appreciate in nut tree (9)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start to a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: macadam is a smooth road surface

annotation.surface: Admiring the smooth bark of a nut tree.
annotation.walkthrough: Macadam is a road surface of compacted broken stone, named after John McAdam.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an Australian evergreen grown commercially for its round, rich nuts.

entries.clue: People with an opinion about origin of conflict in mad character in spectacles (10,7)

indicatorNotes.origin: the origin of something is where it begins, so the first letter of conflict
indicatorNotes.in: this first 'in' puts the conflict's letter inside the spectacles

blocks.note: the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland
first letter of Conflict, put inside GLASSES

annotation.surface: Opinionated people discussing how a conflict started while a madman wears glasses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it links the definition to its subject, but it gives C; the second 'in' is literal and the first places the conflict's C.
annotation.definitionFit: A mildly mocking British term for educated people who love to air their opinions on current affairs.

entries.clue: Drug is found following arrest behind prison (8)

indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so IS comes after the arrest
indicatorNotes.behind: behind means after in reading order, so the arrest comes after the prison

annotation.surface: Drugs turn up after an arrest, and the suspect ends up behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards from the answer: the last word gives the first piece. 'is found' does double duty, supplying IS and linking.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the narcotic made from the hemp plant, also called marijuana.

entries.clue: Critical comments picked up in A&E, being perceptive (6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: something picked up is lifted, and in a down entry a lifted word reads bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed word sits in between A and E

blocks.note: the letters A and E, around the reversed word

annotation.surface: Staff in a hospital emergency department hear critical remarks and show insight.
annotation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room, but here it only supplies its two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shrewd, quick to see what is really going on.

entries.clue: Annoyance after losing last old currency (4)

indicatorNotes.after losing last: a word that has lost its last has lost its final letter

blocks.note: PEST, an annoyance, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Irritation at losing the last of an old currency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'old currency' looks like one phrase for the definition; 'old' is O and the peso is still in use.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the money of Mexico, the Philippines and several South American countries.

entries.clue: A stream running through a second Texan city (8)

indicatorNotes.running through: a stream runs through a landscape, so A RILL runs through the middle of MO

blocks.note: a as written, the second one in the clue
a mo is a moment, a second
A + RILL, a rill being a small stream

annotation.surface: A second brook flows through a Texas city.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue's first A travels with the stream into MO; the second, 'a second', stays in front.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the largest city of the Texas Panhandle.

entries.clue: Little daughter beside jetty, abandoned by husband (5)

indicatorNotes.beside: beside means next to, so D stands next to the jetty
indicatorNotes.abandoned by: a jetty abandoned by the husband has lost its H

blocks.note: WHARF, a jetty, without H for husband

annotation.surface: A small daughter left on a quay by her husband.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little daughter' looks like one phrase; 'Little' is the definition, used as an adjective for a dwarf plant or star.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in dwarf conifer or dwarf star, it means undersized.

entries.clue: Passion in a lot of football teams means: ‘Shoot!’ (4,4)

indicatorNotes.in: the passion is placed in, inside, the letters FA

blocks.note: the FA, the Football Association, governs a great many English teams

annotation.surface: A football chant urging a striker to shoot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like the link to the definition, but it gives WAY; 'Shoot!' is the everyday invitation to speak.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both are informal invitations to go ahead and say what you want to say.

entries.clue: Tolkien character? Try to think back (6)

indicatorNotes.back: thinking back means going backwards, so the word for think is read backwards

blocks.note: to have a go is to try

annotation.surface: Trying to recall a character from Tolkien.
annotation.walkthrough: Gollum is the creature from The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ring-obsessed creature of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

entries.clue: Refine jet design, perhaps, lest airmen crashed (10)

indicatorNotes.crashed: a crashed plane is wrecked, so the letters of the airmen are wrecked and rearranged

annotation.surface: Improving an aircraft's shape so the pilots don't crash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the jet as one example of what can be streamlined.
annotation.definitionFit: Shaping an aircraft to cut air resistance is streamlining in its original, literal sense.

entries.clue: Underwear I have incorporating left and right leg? I’m missing one (4,4,6)

indicatorNotes.incorporating: to incorporate is to take into the body, so I'VE takes the L into itself

blocks.note: R = right, added at the end

annotation.surface: Someone describes their long underwear, with a leg missing.
annotation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate of Treasure Island, so the definition is spoken in his voice.
annotation.definitionFit: The pirate of Treasure Island has only one leg, so asked about a leg he might well say he's missing one.

entries.clue: Where’s most of the dictionary when everything’s accounted for? (5,3)

blocks.note: alphabetically, the word 'all' comes early, so most entries follow it
a phrase meaning in the end, all things considered

annotation.surface: Asking where the bulk of a dictionary lies once every entry has been counted.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint: 'all' starts early in any dictionary, so most entries come after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally placed later than the word 'all', and the idiom meaning once everything is taken into account.

entries.clue: Work beginning to manifest death to ruler, King? (2,5,7)

annotation.definition: Work beginning to manifest death to ruler, King?

indicatorNotes.Work: read as a command, to work something is to knead it into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped
indicatorNotes.beginning: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A literary work that opens by foretelling the death of a king.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur is a work that shows the death of the ruler King Arthur.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes Malory's romance, whose French title means 'the death of Arthur', the king.

entries.clue: Huge number turned up, a number unspecified for delivery worker (8)

indicatorNotes.turned up: turned upward means flipped to read bottom to top, which in a down entry is backwards

blocks.note: n is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

annotation.surface: A crowd shows up, some unspecified number of them, waiting on a delivery driver.
annotation.walkthrough: The delivery worker is a milkman; dairymen delivered milk door to door.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a dairyman sells milk, and in Britain traditionally delivered it to the door each morning.

entries.clue: Cancels credit offered in regular payments (6)

indicatorNotes.offered in: something offered in is put inside, so the credit goes inside the payments

annotation.surface: Cancelling a credit arrangement offered on a subscription.
annotation.walkthrough: To scrub a plan is to cancel it, a mostly British informal sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Informally, to scrub a launch or plan is to call it off, as if wiping it from the board.

entries.clue: Location of capital often a holiday destination (6,2,6)

annotation.definition: Location of capital often a holiday destination

blocks.note: capital means money here, not a seat of government
travellers visit before a trip abroad to buy foreign notes

annotation.surface: A capital city that doubles as a popular tourist resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a seat of government; it is money, and holidaymakers head to a bureau de change for foreign currency.
annotation.definitionFit: An office where money is exchanged is a place full of capital, and holidaymakers often call there first.

entries.clue: China cabal disrupted a historic festivity (11)

indicatorNotes.disrupted: something disrupted is thrown out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a as written, also in the fodder

annotation.surface: A plotting clique in China breaks up an ancient celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bacchanalia were Roman festivals of Bacchus, god of wine; the word now means any drunken revelry.
annotation.definitionFit: The Roman festival of Bacchus, god of wine, a historic occasion of feasting and drinking.

entries.clue: Lower area of land occupied by graduate negotiator (8)

indicatorNotes.occupied by: land occupied by someone has them inside it, so MA sits inside LOT

blocks.note: a lot is a plot of land

annotation.surface: A graduate negotiator settles on a low-lying stretch of land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as an adjective describing the land; it is a verb, DIP.
annotation.definitionFit: An official whose job is to negotiate with foreign governments on their country's behalf.

entries.clue: Most of latest styles arranged insipidly (11)

indicatorNotes.Most of: most of a word is all but its end, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.arranged: arranging is putting in a chosen order, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder with LATES, 11 letters in all

annotation.surface: Most of the latest fashions have been put together dully.
annotation.walkthrough: Only 'latest' is shortened; 'styles' goes in whole.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: insipid food has no flavour, and so does food prepared tastelessly.

entries.clue: Philosopher identified in girl’s account on literature (American) (10)

indicatorNotes.on: on means placed upon, and in a down entry the account sits on top of the literature

annotation.surface: A philosopher named in a girl's report on American literature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'girl's' gives HER, the possessive pronoun, rather than a girl's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Greek thinker of Ephesus who taught that everything is in flux.

entries.clue: Auctions go astray, affecting contacts (10)

indicatorNotes.go astray: things that go astray wander off their proper course, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters; 'go' serves as fodder and as part of the indicator

annotation.surface: Sales going wrong hurt the dealers' business connections.
annotation.walkthrough: 'go' does double duty, both in the fodder and in the instruction 'go astray'.
annotation.definitionFit: A disease that spreads by touch is passed to, and affects, the people its carrier comes into contact with.

entries.clue: Best to accept new response, all the same (9)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so IDEAL takes in the new response

blocks.note: the ideal is the best possible
a tic is an involuntary response

annotation.surface: Best to accept the new answer, whatever it is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'all the same' reads as 'nevertheless'; here it means exactly alike.
annotation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike in every respect are all the same as one another.

entries.clue: Buffalo Bill enthrals me — light entertainment (6)

indicatorNotes.enthrals: to enthral originally meant to hold in thrall, captive, so CODY holds ME captive

annotation.surface: Buffalo Bill's Wild West show captivates me with its light fun.
annotation.walkthrough: Buffalo Bill was the showman William F. Cody, who toured his Wild West show.
annotation.definitionFit: Funny plays and shows are the classic form of light, rather than serious, entertainment.

entries.clue: Safe haven — at first, only what it seems (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: at first means at the very beginning, so only the first letter of only

blocks.note: as is = in its present state, just what it seems

annotation.surface: A safe haven that at first is only what it appears, perhaps a mirage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a mirage, the oasis that is only what it seems.
annotation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a fertile spot in the desert stands for any place of refuge from hardship.

entries.clue: Hard alcohol’s source: Prohibition Era dance (8)

indicatorNotes.source: a source is where something springs from, so the first letter of alcohol

annotation.surface: Strong drink's supplier during the Prohibition years, and a dance of the period.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prohibition Era' reads as the American 1920s, and 'Hard alcohol' as spirits; each word works alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a slow Cuban dance in duple time, famous from Carmen.

entries.clue: Surprise without opening wine (4)

indicatorNotes.without opening: a word without its opening has lost its first letter

blocks.note: SHOCK, a surprise, without its first letter S

annotation.surface: A surprise: a bottle of wine left unopened.
annotation.walkthrough: Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term for German white wine, from Hochheim on the Main.

entries.clue: Composer’s name is translated — French are engaged in that (8)

indicatorNotes.translated: to translate is to change into another form, so the letters change into a new order
indicatorNotes.engaged in: someone engaged in an activity is inside it, so ES goes inside the mixed letters

annotation.surface: A French composer's name is translated, with French speakers involved in the work.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Composer is [the wordplay]. Olivier Messiaen was a French composer, which the French words hint at.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Olivier Messiaen wrote the Quartet for the End of Time and the Turangalila Symphony.

entries.clue: Height in a border may be an Alpine problem? (9)

indicatorNotes.in: height is placed in, inside, the border

blocks.note: a valance is a decorative border of fabric

annotation.surface: Mountain height on a frontier could cause Alpine difficulties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a national frontier in the Alps; it is a valance, the fabric trim round a bed or curtain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: snow sliding down steep slopes is a well-known hazard in the Alps.

entries.clue: Five line verse scheme including half line for Arabian hero (3,4)

indicatorNotes.including: a scheme including something takes it in, so ABABA takes LI inside
indicatorNotes.half: half a line is half of the word line, its first two letters

blocks.note: ABABA is a five-line rhyme scheme

annotation.surface: A poet planning a five-line poem, with half a line for a hero of Arabian tales.
annotation.walkthrough: A rhyme scheme is written as letters, one per line; five lines rhyming ABABA give the frame.
annotation.definitionFit: The woodcutter of the Forty Thieves tale is a hero of the Arabian Nights.

entries.clue: Revolutionary period taking head of the old Queen, King and heads of other royals (6)

indicatorNotes.head: the head of a word is its top, which in a down entry is its first letter
indicatorNotes.heads: the heads of the words other and royals are their first letters

blocks.note: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
first letters of Other and Royals

annotation.surface: A revolution in which the old queen, the king and other royals lose their heads.
annotation.walkthrough: The Terror was the phase of the French Revolution when the king, queen and many nobles were guillotined, so the surface fits the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Terror is the name given to the bloodiest stretch of the French Revolution, 1793 to 1794.

entries.clue: Are resident in home, like family members, often (7)

indicatorNotes.resident in: a resident lives inside a home, so ARE lives inside NEST

annotation.surface: Living at home, as relatives often do.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the phrase 'nearest and dearest', meaning family.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: one's nearest and dearest are one's close family.

entries.clue: Likely charge netting pounds to cover a blood relative (8)

indicatorNotes.netting: a net catches and holds, so FEE holds the rest inside it
indicatorNotes.to cover: to cover something is to hold it in, so the pounds hold a blood relative

annotation.surface: A plausible bill includes money to pay for a relative.
annotation.walkthrough: A double inclusion: A SIB sits inside L, and that sits inside FEE; the L lands after the SIB.
annotation.definitionFit: In a looser sense the word means plausible, as in a feasible explanation, which is a likely one.

entries.clue: Enjoyable days disposing of core reserves? (5)

indicatorNotes.disposing of core: the core is the middle, as of an apple, so the middle letters are thrown away

blocks.note: fun is an adjective for enjoyable

annotation.surface: Pleasant days spent using up core savings.
annotation.walkthrough: The core of DAYS is its middle two letters, AY.
annotation.definitionFit: Money set aside for use is held in reserve, so the question mark admits a loose synonym.

entries.clue: Sorceress adopting line — one in London? (6)

indicatorNotes.adopting: to adopt is to take in as one's own, so the sorceress takes in the L

blocks.note: Circe is the enchantress of Homer's Odyssey

annotation.surface: A sorceress taking up a line, a witch in London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'line': the Circle line is a London Underground line.
annotation.definitionFit: The one refers back to 'line': the Circle is a London Underground line.

entries.clue: What indicates debt in company? This is what I believe (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the debt colour is placed in, inside, the company

blocks.note: red ink shows a debt, being 'in the red'

annotation.surface: Asking what shows debt in a firm, then stating a creed.
annotation.walkthrough: Credo is Latin for 'I believe', which the definition paraphrases.
annotation.definitionFit: The Latin word means 'I believe' and names a statement of belief, which this definition paraphrases.

entries.clue: Hot and largely scented Indian festival (4)

indicatorNotes.largely: largely means for the most part, not wholly, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: OLID, strong-smelling, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A hot and fragrant Indian celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: Olid is a rare word for foul-smelling, so 'scented' means smelly rather than perfumed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Hindu spring festival where people throw coloured powder.

entries.clue: Failure nearer, after yielding lead (5)

indicatorNotes.after yielding lead: a runner yielding the lead gives up the front position, so the front letter goes

blocks.note: CLOSER, nearer, without its first letter C

annotation.surface: A runner who gave up the lead fails as the finish nears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as a racing lead; it is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe a person who habitually fails, a sense of failure applied to people.

entries.clue: Discussion topics, say, implementing switch in limits to visitors for wildlife protection zones (12,5)

indicatorNotes.implementing switch in: to switch two things is to swap their places, so the V and S change places

blocks.note: conversation areas: topics of discussion, 'say' marking a loose phrase
the outer letters of VisitorS, which swap in CONVERSATION

annotation.surface: Topics to discuss with visitors to nature reserves, such as the rules on where they may go.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the V and S of CONVERSATION and it becomes CONSERVATION.
annotation.definitionFit: Loosely defined: in Britain these are officially protected districts, and the phrase fits land kept for wildlife too.

entries.clue: Large southern area sadly blocking European country (11)

indicatorNotes.blocking: something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it, so ALAS sits in the middle of the country

annotation.surface: A big southern region sadly shut out of a European country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'sadly' is not an anagram indicator here; it gives ALAS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the region of Australia, New Zealand and nearby Pacific islands, south of the equator.

entries.clue: Soldiers with tale about irrational gunners getting out of breath (11)

indicatorNotes.about: about means surrounding, so the tale surrounds the irrational gunners

annotation.surface: Soldiers telling tales about crazed gunners are left breathless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'irrational' reads as describing the gunners, but it is a noun: PI, the irrational number.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to breathing, so it is literally 'of breath'.
